children: Wizz Air has been rocked by engine issues, conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East, and Covid-19. The £1 bln carrier’s 2030 targets suggest fleet growth below prior goals, and margins lower than in its heyday. With fuel costs soaring and rivals retrenching, caution makes sense.
Full view will be published shortly.
Wizz Air held a capital markets day and announced medium-term goals on September 17.
The London-listed airline said its targets for the financial year ending March 2030 included revenue of €10 billion, an operating margin of 10%, and an investment-grade balance sheet.

Wizz also said that summer trading had been better than expected, with so-called revenue per available seat kilometre in its second quarter guided to flat year-on-year, versus “down low single digits” previously.
Shares in Wizz rose 3.4% on September 17. They are up around 9% since their close on September 16.
